newsitem.title: USA: US Senate votes against next round of base closings.
newsitem.headline: US Senate votes against next round of base closings.

text.p: The U.S. Senate voted on Wednesday night to delay the next two rounds of military base closings sought by the Defense Department.
The vote, which crossed party lines, was 66-33. The vote was on an amendment to the $262 billion defense spending bill, which the Senate hopes to complete work on this week.

The amendment, sponsored by Sen. Byron Dorgan, a Democrat from North Dakota, and Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott, would allow already authorized base closures to go ahead, but it would not allow another round of domestic base closures until at least 2001.

The amendment requires the Pentagon to prepare a more thorough accounting of how much the closures actually save before Congress authorized another round of controversial and politically difficult shutdowns, which can economically damage communities that are near the base.
The House already passed its version of the defense bill, omitting the authorization of base closings.
Secretary of Defense William Cohen had wanted two more rounds of base closures in 1999 and 2001, partly to help pay for billions of dollars in high-tech weaponry for the 21st century.
